sections.title: Embodied Interfaces for Immersion
sections.description: “Embodied Interfaces for Immersion” explores the design of Natural User Interfaces (NUIs) for Extended Realities (VR, AR, Projection Mapping) to create immersive, human-centered, and embodied experiences in physical and virtual spaces. NUIs in this context not only aim to lower cognitive load but also serve as creative tools for crafting fluid, expressive, and accessible interactions. Students will explore artistic approaches to interface design, working with a range of technologies like spatial computing, circuit bending, scripting, and fabrication, to construct human-centered, inclusive interfaces that enable meaningful, artistic experiences that deepen the connection between users and their surrounding environment.

sections.title: Embodied Interfaces for Immersion
sections.description:
“Embodied Interfaces: Experiential Art and Design” explores the design of Interactive Interfaces that feel invisible and mimic human behaviors like touch, voice and gesture (Natural User Interfaces) for Interactive experiences. Rather than treating ease-of-use as the only goal, the course frames physical interface design as an artistic practice and invites students to re-focus on the embodied, social, and shared experience of technology, drawing from a rich lineage of game and UX design and participatory art practices.
Alternative, body-driven interfaces are presented as a way to create connection between people: through play, creative expression, and community-building. Students work with a range of technology -- including motion and spatial tracking(spatial computing), modified electronics(circuit bending), code, and physical fabrication -- to design human-centered interfaces that feel intuitive, welcome a wide range of users, and produce experiences that strengthen the relationship between a person and their surrounding environment.
